stories.headline: Any terror attack originating from Pakistan will invite stronger response: Rajnath Singh
stories.title: Any terror attack originating from Pakistan will invite stronger response: Rajnath Singh
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 15: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday said any terrorist act originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response from India, asserting that Operation Sindoor, the Balakot airstrikes and surgical strikes marked a shift from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action against terrorism. Addressing a Defence Conclave in New Delhi, Singh said India remained committed to peace but its commitment should not be mistaken for weakness. “Our commitment to peace remains steadfast, yet we are fully prepared to confront any challenge,” he said, adding that India was determined to safeguard its sovereignty, territorial integrity and national interests. Singh said the three military operations symbolised India's approach of targeting the sources of terrorism rather than limiting its response to diplomatic condemnation. He also claimed that since 2014, the “shelf life” of most terrorists had fallen to less than a year, with security forces neutralising them within a year of taking up arms against India. Highlighting the changing security landscape, the Defence Minister warned of emerging threats, including lone-wolf attacks and what he described as “white-collar terrorism”. He said terrorism was evolving beyond organised groups, making it increasingly difficult for security agencies to identify radicalised individuals and prevent potential attacks. Singh also referred to the recent incident involving a co-pilot who allegedly attempted to crash a passenger aircraft and Indian Captain Smit Machchhar, who risked his life to avert a major disaster. He said the incident highlighted the threat posed by lone-wolf attackers and underscored the importance of alert and responsible citizens in preventing terrorist plots. “The fight against terrorism requires not only the capabilities of security agencies but also the active participation of aware and responsible citizens,” he said. Singh described the emerging security environment as one characterised by hybrid, high-tech and hyper warfare. He identified what he termed the “5D Security Threat” — disinformation, destabilisation, disruption, deception and destruction — and called for greater vigilance and preparedness. On defence preparedness, the minister called for a “smart power” approach that combines advanced weaponry, artificial intelligence, human intelligence and cost-effective technologies to address evolving security challenges. He said India needed to integrate precision-guided weapons and loitering munitions with affordable, agile and adaptable systems to strengthen its defence capabilities. Singh attributed India's growing defence capabilities to reforms undertaken under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, saying the government had shifted its focus from meeting immediate military requirements to building a self-reliant and future-ready defence ecosystem. He said defence production had increased to a record level of over Rs 1.78 lakh crore from around Rs 40,000 crore in 2014, while defence exports had risen to an all-time high of Rs 39,000 crore from Rs 686 crore in 2013-14. Indian defence products, he said, were now reaching nearly 100 countries. The minister expressed confidence that India would achieve defence production worth Rs 2 lakh crore in the current year and Rs 3 lakh crore by 2029, while targeting defence exports worth Rs 50,000 crore by the same year. Emphasising domestic manufacturing, Singh said more than 500 companies were engaged in the defence sector, while over 16,000 micro, small and medium enterprises were contributing to the country's defence industrial ecosystem. He said the government had earmarked 75 per cent of the defence modernisation budget for procurement from Indian industries and highlighted initiatives to promote indigenous defence equipment and technology. Singh also highlighted the role of start-ups and young innovators in developing drones, artificial intelligence, quantum technology, cybersecurity and robotics. He said the Ministry of Defence had approved procurement of goods and services worth over Rs 2,400 crore from start-ups and MSMEs and sanctioned projects worth more than Rs 1,500 crore for developing new technologies. The minister said India was steadily progressing towards self-reliance in defence manufacturing, with 159 of the 175 ammunition variants used by the armed forces now being produced domestically. Singh concluded by expressing confidence that India would emerge as a developed nation by the centenary of its independence and provide global leadership in technology, the economy and defence.

New Delhi, October 15: Reiterating India’s stand on cross-border terrorism, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday asserted that any further terrorist acts originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response.
He emphasised that while India’s cultural ethos favoured dialogue, coexistence and peaceful resolution of disputes, its commitment to peace should not be mistaken for weakness.

“Operation Sindoor, Balakot Airstrikes and Surgical Strikes weren’t just military operations; they symbolised a decisive shift in the nation’s approach, moving from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action aimed at rooting out terrorism by reaching its very source,” Singh said at the Times Network Defence Conclave in New Delhi.

Defence Minister termed strength and capability as essential to maintaining peace, and underlined that India hopes for peace, but remains prepared for war that sometimes becomes necessary to protect the nation.
“Our commitment to peace remains steadfast, yet we are fully prepared to confront any challenge.

Our goal is to build an India that, while advocating for peace, remains vigilant when it comes to security and is fully capable of safeguarding its sovereignty, integrity, and national interests,” he said.
On the evolving security landscape, Singh underscored the need for heightened vigilance and preparedness in an era of hybrid, high-tech and hyper warfare.

He highlighted the growing complexity of security threats in the digital age, identifying what he described as the ‘5D Security Threat ’-Disinformation, Destabilisation, Disruption, Deception and Destruction.

He pointed out that terrorism was evolving beyond organised groups, and emerging threats include ‘lone-wolf’ attacks and ‘white-collar terrorism’, which make it increasingly difficult for security agencies to identify radicalised individuals and prevent potential attacks.

The Defence Minister referred to the recent incident involving a co-pilot who allegedly attempted to crash a passenger aircraft and Captain Smit Machhar who risked his life to avert a major terror attack.
“The incident underscored the threat posed by lone-wolf attackers while demonstrating how the courage and commitment of an individual could thwart the designs of those driven by hatred.
A single alert and courageous individual could help foil an entire terrorist plot.
On defence preparedness, Singh underscored the need to combine ‘hard power’ with ‘soft power’ and called for a shift towards ‘smart power’.

“Modern defence strategies must integrate precision-guided weapons and loitering munitions with cost-effective weaponry, human intelligence with artificial intelligence, and advanced systems with low-cost, agile and adaptable technologies to address evolving security challenges,” he said.

On the growth witnessed by the defence sector due to the Government’s efforts, Singh stated that defence production has risen to a record over Rs 1.78 lakh crore from Rs 40,000 crore in 2014, with defence exports touching an all-time high of Rs 39,000 crore from Rs 686 crore in 2013-14, and India defence products reaching nearly 100 countries.

He exuded confidence that the nation would achieve defence production targets of Rs 2 lakh crore this year and Rs 3 lakh crore by 2029, and export defence equipment worth Rs 50,000 crore by 2029, the Ministry said in its statement.

The Defence Minister attributed the growth to reforms that simplified export procedures, including the introduction of the Defence EXIM Portal, online approvals, the Open General Export License, streamlined quality certification and the ‘Green Channel’ policy.
These measures, he said, enhanced India’s global credibility and prepared domestic industries to compete in international markets.

"The Ministry of Defence has approved procurement of goods and services worth over Rs 2,400 crore from start-ups and MSMEs and sanctioned projects exceeding Rs 1,500 crore for new technology development.
As of March 2026, iDEX had engaged 676 start-ups and innovators and facilitated the signing of 551 contracts.

From a few dozen defence startups in 2018, the ecosystem had grown to more than 2,000, with young enterprises working across drones, artificial intelligence, quantum technology, cybersecurity, robotics and other advanced fields,” he added.

Citing progress in ammunition manufacturing, he said 159 of the 175 ammunition variants used by the Defence Forces were now indigenously produced, representing more than 90 per cent self-reliance in ammunition variants.

Referring to India’s exports of bulletproof jackets to over 100 countries, he noted that the country was the fourth in the world to establish a national standard for bulletproof jackets aligned with international norms.
He also spoke about the implementation of the One Rank.
One Pension scheme and the creation of the Chief of Defence Staff post, terming them significant measures undertaken to strengthen the defence framework.

stories.headline: Assam: Despite Losing Both Legs in Train Accident, Artisan Crafts 16 Durga Idols
stories.title: Assam: Despite Losing Both Legs in Train Accident, Artisan Crafts 16 Durga Idols
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'train accident' in title weight 64
article_sentences: Guwahati: As preparations for Durga Puja gather pace across Assam, the inspiring story of a differently abled artisan from Cachar district has captured attention.
Montu Pal, a resident of Siddheswar village in Katigorah, has been crafting Durga idols for the past 18 years, overcoming severe physical challenges through determination and dedication to his art.
Pal lost both his legs in a horrific train accident several years ago.
While the tragedy could have shattered his spirit, it failed to diminish his passion for idol-making.
Undeterred by his physical limitations, he continued his artistic journey, working on his knees and crawling to shape clay into beautifully crafted idols.
Throughout this challenging journey, Pal has received unwavering support from his family.
His wife and children have stood firmly by his side, assisting him at every stage of the idol-making process.
Their contribution has enabled him to continue pursuing his craft despite the difficulties he faces.
This year, Pal has created 16 Durga idols entirely by hand for the upcoming festival, reflecting his exceptional craftsmanship and perseverance.
However, rising prices of raw materials have added to his financial difficulties.
The cost of essential materials, including paint, bamboo, straw, sand and clay, has reportedly nearly doubled, significantly increasing the expenses involved in making the idols.
Despite these challenges, Pal remains committed to his work.

stories.headline: Election Commission announces voter list revision in 17 states, SIR schedule to follow
stories.title: Election Commission announces voter list revision in 17 states, SIR schedule to follow
stories.summary: In a notice issued on Thursday, the Election Commission directed the states and Union Territories to conduct the revision under Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, with January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The revision will cover Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal.
The Commission said the schedule for SSR in states and Union Territories where the SIR exercise is ongoing or has recently been completed would be announced separately.
The announcement comes amid a legal challenge to the SIR process.

The Supreme Court recently issued notices to the ECI, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on a petition filed by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders.

The petition challenges the legality of the SIR exercise and seeks disclosure of the Election Commission’s records, publication of details of deleted voters and safeguards against arbitrary deletions.

The petitioners have also sought a mechanism to restore names removed from electoral rolls, a judicial audit of the revision process and suspension of the exercise across states until the case is decided.

The petition was filed by Gandhi along with Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Trinamool Congress leader Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, RJD leader Tejashwi Prasad Yadav and other opposition leaders representing parties across the INDIA bloc.

The group also includes Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut, CPI(M) leader MA Baby, CPI leader D Raja, JMM leader Mahua Majhi, NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar faction) leader Supriya Sule, IUML leader Mohammed Basheer, VCK president Thol.
Thirumavalavan and former Jammu and Kashmir minister Sajjad Ahmad Kichloo.
The legal challenge followed an Opposition march towards the Supreme Court on October 12, led by Gandhi, to protest against the SIR exercise.

Opposition leaders had earlier sought an appointment with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to raise concerns about the process and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The CJI declined the request, noting that the issues were already pending before the court and that the leaders could seek relief through judicial proceedings.

stories.headline: RJD MP Manoj Jha Moves Supreme Court Challenging Lifelong Immunity To CEC, Election Commissioners; Calls It 'Fraud On Constitution'
stories.title: RJD MP Manoj Jha Moves Supreme Court Challenging Lifelong Immunity To CEC, Election Commissioners; Calls It 'Fraud On Constitution'
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha has approached the Supreme Court challenging the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, terming it a "fraud" on the Constitution.

Section 16 bars every Court in the country from entertaining or continuing any civil or criminal proceeding against any person who is or was a Chief Election Commissioner or Election Commissioner, for anything done "or purporting" to be done in the discharge of official duty.

Jha has stated that Section 16 confers on unelected officials a shield/blanket immunity which is not even extended to the President, Governor, Member of Parliament, State Legislature, or any judge of the Supreme Court or the High Court, because the immunity extends for a lifetime.
This was added through an amendment in 2023, which had also removed the pro tem arrangement made by the Supreme Court in Anoop Baranwal.

Union of India(2023) for the appointment of the CEC by a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or the leader of the largest opposition party), and the Chief Justice of India.
The 2023 Act had removed the CJI and added a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.

Jha's petition argues: "Parliament, by a late official amendment to an ordinary Bill, has handed the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners a protection wider than all of them: civil and criminal, during office and for life after it, with no carve-out for corruption, mala fides or crime, and with no authority anywhere empowered to lift it."
Jha has stated that Section 16, added through an amendment, is a fraud on the Constitution because it was not originally provided in the Act.
He has said that wherever the Constitutional framers thought fit to provide functional immunity, it has done so and that too only till the person is holding the office.
Per contra, no such immunity was provided under Section 324 of the Constitution for the protection of the Election Commission.
"Section 16 nonetheless confers a constitutional-grade immunity, larger than any the Constitution grants or permits, through a simple majority statute.
It does so under the label of "conditions of service" in an Act whose long title speaks only of "appointment, conditions of service and term of office" and "transaction of business".

stories.headline: Ladakh has seen major infrastructure transformation under PM Modi's leadership: LG Saxena
stories.title: Ladakh has seen major infrastructure transformation under PM Modi's leadership: LG Saxena
stories.summary: Leh, Oct 15: Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena hailed the Centre's initiatives on Thursday after Prime Minister Narendra Modi virtually inaugurated five development projects in Ladakh, including airport infrastructure and strategic road connectivity, worth around Rs 3,350 crore. Saxena said the region has seen a major transformation in infrastructure and living standards under the Prime Minister's leadership since it became a Union Territory in 2019. Saxena said, "Five new infrastructure projects would prove to be milestones in Ladakh's development, strengthening connectivity, water security, power supply and preservation of cultural heritage." The Lieutenant Governor (LG) thanked Narendra Modi for his leadership and support, saying the people of Ladakh's seven districts looked forward to his address with high hopes and aspirations. The Prime Minister inaugurated five projects, including a modern passenger terminal at Leh airport; the Nimmu-Padam-Darcha road connecting the Zanskar valley; India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park in Leh; the 9 MW Hanu Hydroelectric Project; and power transmission infrastructure and 35 water bodies under the Amrit Sarovar initiative. "The inauguration of the Banga Bot Kharu Small Hydroelectric Project and the 66-kV Thahanu-Khalsti transmission line will also help strengthen the region's power infrastructure," the LG said. Saxena said the new airport terminal would improve air connectivity and passenger facilities, particularly during winter, while the Nimmu-Padam-Darcha road would connect remote areas with the mainstream of development and strengthen internal security. Highlighting 2019, he said granting Ladakh Union Territory status fulfilled a long-standing demand for a distinct identity and greater recognition. "The formation of five new districts in April this year and the recent approval for establishing Autonomous Hill Development Councils in all seven districts were important steps towards fulfilling local aspirations," he said. Saxena said Ladakh was improving road connectivity and other infrastructure, while work under the Jal Jeevan Mission was progressing to provide clean drinking water to households despite sub-zero temperatures. He said new policies were also being introduced to economically empower Pashmina herders, while agricultural diversification was helping increase farmers' incomes. The LG said Ladakh, which once depended on outside supplies for vegetables, now has more than 11,000 greenhouses where farmers grow vegetables locally and supply them to defence forces through cooperatives. Emphasising the importance of water conservation, Saxena said initiatives such as Amrit Him Sarovar and conserving glacial water resources were helping ensure long-term water security in the strategically important region. Improved connectivity, infrastructure development, and ease of doing business have also boosted tourism and strengthened the local economy, he said. The LG said the Zojila Tunnel's completion would address one of Ladakh's major connectivity challenges, as the region often remains cut off from the rest of the country during winter due to heavy snowfall. Work on the tunnel is progressing on a war footing, he said, and he requested the Prime Minister to inaugurate the project once it was completed. Saxena expressed confidence that Ladakh would continue to receive the Prime Minister's guidance and support for its overall development. He welcomed Modi on behalf of the Ladakh administration and its people, thanking him for participating in the programme despite being unable to visit the region in person. "The snow-covered peaks and the inaccessible valleys of Ladakh have always symbolised courage and perseverance. However, under the leadership of the Prime Minister, these very challenges have now become symbols of development and new hope," Saxena said. He said Modi's decision to join the programme virtually reflected his affection for the people of Ladakh, his dedication to their welfare and his vision for the region. Saxena said the people of Ladakh would remain grateful to the Prime Minister for sparing his valuable time to honour them and give unprecedented momentum to the region's development. Ladakh is home to hundreds of prehistoric rock art sites featuring carvings of wildlife, human figures and symbolic representations that offer valuable insights into thousands of years of human history.

Improved connectivity, infrastructure development, and ease of doing business have also boosted tourism and strengthened the local economy, he said.

The LG said the Zojila Tunnel's completion would address one of Ladakh's major connectivity challenges, as the region often remains cut off from the rest of the country during winter due to heavy snowfall.
Work on the tunnel is progressing on a war footing, he said, and he requested the Prime Minister to inaugurate the project once it was completed.
Saxena expressed confidence that Ladakh would continue to receive the Prime Minister's guidance and support for its overall development.
He welcomed Modi on behalf of the Ladakh administration and its people, thanking him for participating in the programme despite being unable to visit the region in person.
"The snow-covered peaks and the inaccessible valleys of Ladakh have always symbolised courage and perseverance.
However, under the leadership of the Prime Minister, these very challenges have now become symbols of development and new hope," Saxena said.
He said Modi's decision to join the programme virtually reflected his affection for the people of Ladakh, his dedication to their welfare and his vision for the region.
Saxena said the people of Ladakh would remain grateful to the Prime Minister for sparing his valuable time to honour them and give unprecedented momentum to the region's development.

Ladakh is home to hundreds of prehistoric rock art sites featuring carvings of wildlife, human figures and symbolic representations that offer valuable insights into thousands of years of human history.

The Prime Minister inaugurated five projects, including a modern passenger terminal at Leh airport; the Nimmu-Padam-Darcha road connecting the Zanskar valley; India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park in Leh; the 9 MW Hanu Hydroelectric Project; and power transmission infrastructure and 35 water bodies under the Amrit Sarovar initiative.

"The formation of five new districts in April this year and the recent approval for establishing Autonomous Hill Development Councils in all seven districts were important steps towards fulfilling local aspirations," he said.
Saxena said, "Five new infrastructure projects would prove to be milestones in Ladakh's development, strengthening connectivity, water security, power supply and preservation of cultural heritage."

It’s down to that kind of detail,” he explained.India signed a trade deal with the European Union earlier this year, which was concluded after 20 years of negotiations. article_sentences: The Supreme Court sought the Election Commission's response to an Opposition petition challenging electoral roll revisions.
It also warned political leaders against attempting to pressure the judiciary through protests or public statements.

The Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Election Commission and its chief, Gyanesh Kumar, to respond to a petition filed by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and 12 other Opposition leaders alleging large-scale deletion of voters and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
The court also took strong note of claims that Gandhi and others had attempted to pressure the judiciary by holding a march on October 12.
It issued notices to Gandhi and several other Opposition leaders over the march.
“Nobody can browbeat us,” Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said, adding that the bench was aware of developments and statements made inside and outside the courtroom.
“We will ask one of the petitioners about his conduct on the next date of hearing,” the CJI said without naming anyone.
The observation came after a state unit of the Congress recently sought the CJI's resignation while commenting on his statement that law and order fell within the executive's domain.
“We are not sitting in ivory towers.
We know what statements they are making outside and what they are saying in court.
We know everything,” the CJI said.
He was heading a bench that also included Justice Joymalya Bagchi, according to PTI.

article_sentences: The first tranche of the India-US bilateral trade agreement has been finalised and is undergoing legal drafting, Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday.
He added that it would be operationalised once India secures a comparable tariff advantage.
“The first tranche of the US bilateral trade agreement has been finalised.

It is going through the final contours and legal drafting, and we hope to finalise it soon and operationalise it once we secure a comparable or competitive advantage over our peer countries… These remarks are consistent with exactly what I said yesterday, a week ago and three months ago.
So, there is nothing new in that,” Goyal said.

Later in the day, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal said India and the US were close to finalising the first tranche of the bilateral trade deal and that negotiations were moving in the right direction.
“We are in a very good zone.
We anticipate signing the deal at the earliest,” he told reporters at the monthly trade briefing.
Agarwal, however, underlined that the deal would be finalised only after the tariff structure was settled and there was clarity on the outcome of the Section 301 investigations.
“The tariff structure needs to be finalised.
There is parallel work being done in the US,” he said, adding that the outcome of the Section 301 investigations also needed to be considered.
“A trade deal has a very important component—not only market access, but also preferential market access relative to competitors,” Agarwal noted.

article_sentences: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd (TCS) has launched its Industrial Intelligence Foundry, an AI offering designed to help industrial enterprises scale AI applications across engineering and manufacturing.
Separately, the company announced the completion of its acquisition of a 100% partnership interest in BBY Services India LLP.
The Industrial Intelligence Foundry comprises a repository of configurable AI agents, workflows and governance capabilities.

It is designed to help companies move from AI experimentation to scaled deployment across their value chains, including sectors such as aerospace, mobility, semiconductors, medical devices, industrial electronics, utilities and energy.
TCS shares closed at Rs 2,354.45 on Thursday, up 2.28% from the previous close of Rs 2,302.
The stock opened at Rs 2,354.10, touched a high of Rs 2,386.70 and a low of Rs 2,336.10 during the session.

The offering supports use cases across the product development and manufacturing lifecycle, including engineering intelligence, manufacturing operations optimisation, asset performance, quality and compliance management, and service lifecycle and workforce enablement.
The company said the Foundry can help enterprises reduce new product introduction timelines by 25% and improve manufacturing productivity by 20-25%.
It added that productivity gains could exceed 40% as data foundations and operating ecosystems mature, while maintaining quality, governance and operational performance.

Sreenivasa Chakravarti, global head and vice president of Industrial Autonomy and Engineering at TCS, said, "The next wave of industrial AI will be shaped by how effectively AI agents are orchestrated to transform engineering, plant systems, and asset-centric operations." He added that the company aims to help enterprises deploy domain-specific AI applications at scale and translate industrial knowledge into business outcomes.
In a separate announcement dated October 15, TCS said it had completed the acquisition of a 100% partnership interest in BBY Services India LLP.
The company stated that BBY Services India LLP had become its wholly owned subsidiary with effect from October 15, 2026.

stories.headline: India’s merchandise exports climb 23% to $44.4 bn in September
stories.title: India’s merchandise exports climb 23% to $44.4 bn in September
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 15 : India's merchandise exports recorded a robust 23.04 per cent growth year-on-year to touch a four-month high of $44.4 billion in September this year, despite the uncertainties in global markets and the disruption in shipping due to the escalating Middle East conflict, official figures released on Thursday showed. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal said the growth trend in India's exports was continuing, indicating sustained momentum in outbound shipments. The growth in goods exports was driven by a broad-based increase in shipments across sectors, with particularly strong growth in petroleum products, meat, dairy and poultry products, handicrafts, and some cereals, he added. Imports rose 8 per cent to $74.61 billion during the month due to the increase in prices of crude oil in the global market. The surge in exports also led to a narrowing of the trade deficit to $30.21 billion during the month on a year-on-year basis from around $33 billion recorded in September 2025. However, on a sequential basis, the trade deficit was higher than the corresponding figure of $26.86 billion in the previous month of August. Cumulatively, goods exports stood at $259.89 billion during April-September, up nearly 19 per cent year-on-year. Imports rose 16 per cent year-on-year to $437.53 billion in the first six months of financial year 2026-27 (FY27). As a result, the merchandise trade deficit stood at $177.64 billion during the six-month period. Strong growth in merchandise exports has also increased their contribution to gross domestic product (GDP), after the share of exports recorded a consistent decline over the past three financial years. Exports accounted for 14 per cent of GDP in the first quarter of FY27, the latest figures show. Following a slowdown in global demand in FY24 and FY25, and the uncertainties triggered by the US tariff turmoil in FY26, the share of exports in GDP declined to 11.3 per cent in FY26 from 11.7 per cent in FY25. --IANS

stories.headline: Supreme Court Sets Aside Gift Deed Executed Over Share Given Up In Family Settlement
stories.title: Supreme Court Sets Aside Gift Deed Executed Over Share Given Up In Family Settlement
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has held that a person having parted with his share in a property via a compromise deed cannot later execute a gift deed in relation to the same property.

The Court faulted the Telangana High Court's order for overlooking a compromise deed before upholding the execution of a gift deed by a man who had already relinquished his share via a compromise deed.

A bench of Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva heard a case in which a man, despite having relinquished his claim over properties allotted to his mother under a 1986 compromise in exchange for absolute rights over a house property, subsequently executed a gift deed in 2007 in respect of the same properties.

The core legal issue before the Court was whether a gift deed could be upheld without properly appreciating the effect of an earlier family settlement and a compromise decree that had recognised the parties' respective rights over the properties.
The dispute arose from a family settlement executed on April 19, 1959, dividing ancestral properties among family members.
Under the settlement, Madhusudhan Reddy received specific properties, while certain lands in Karkalpahad village were allotted to his mother, Manikyamma.
Subsequently, during the pendency of litigation concerning the family properties, Madhusudhan Reddy entered into a compromise with Anasuyamma and her adopted son, Venkatraji Reddy, in February 1986.
Under the settlement, he relinquished his claim over the properties allotted to his mother and secured absolute rights over the Himayatnagar house.
The compromise was recorded by the High Court, which allowed the appeal in terms of the settlement in September 1990.
However, in April 2007, Madhusudhan Reddy executed a registered gift deed in favour of Siddhartha Reddy, transferring several parcels of land in Karkalpahad village.

The appellants contended that the lands covered by the deed had not been allotted to Madhusudhan Reddy under the 1959 family settlement and were among the properties over which he had relinquished his claims under the 1986 compromise.

Anasuyamma, Venkatraji Reddy and another family member subsequently filed a suit seeking a declaration of title, a declaration that the gift deed was null and void, mutation of revenue records and a permanent injunction.

Mahadevan and Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya directed the Rajasthan Government and the High Court to recompute the officer's pay under the revised pay scale and release his terminal benefits, including pension and arrears, within three months, subject to there being no other legal impediment.
The case concerned Mukesh Tyagi, who was serving as a Special Judge under the POCSO Act at Dholpur when he granted bail to two accused persons in May 2019.
The Rajasthan High Court subsequently cancelled the bail, observing that no change in circumstances had occurred after the accused persons' earlier bail applications were rejected.

Following the High Court's direction to place its order before the Chief Justice, disciplinary proceedings were initiated against the petitioner-judicial officer under Rule 16 of the Rajasthan Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1958, alleging gross judicial impropriety and indiscipline, following which the petitioner moved the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court declined to interfere with the High Court's observations but separately held that the disciplinary inquiry was unwarranted in the circumstances.
“…in the facts and circumstances of this case, the initiation of an inquiry was not at all required.
Possibly the entry of the remarks of the learned Single Judge in the Annual Confidential Report (ACR) would have sufficed.

We have also stated, the petitioner/judicial officer could have been counseled and warned to be more careful in future and to give sufficient weightage to the orders of the High Court particularly when the same were passed earlier in the same case by the High Court.

In the circumstance, we find that the Memorandum dated 25.10.2024 at Annexure P-6, the statement of charges under Rule 16 of the Rules, the allegation of charge etc. were not warranted for in the instant case.”, the Court held.
The Court also noted that the petitioner's Annual Confidential Reports were positive and that he had retired on March 31, 2026, while his revised pay and terminal benefits remained unreleased.
Accordingly, the Court quashed the disciplinary memorandum dated October 25, 2024, and the related charges.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Sets Aside Orders Rejecting Waqf Trust's Objection To Execution Of Property Decree, Orders Fresh Inquiry
stories.title: Supreme Court Sets Aside Orders Rejecting Waqf Trust's Objection To Execution Of Property Decree, Orders Fresh Inquiry
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has set aside orders rejecting a claim petition filed by Alladin Charities and Zakat Wakf, which sought to resist the execution of a decree for possession of a property in Hyderabad, and remanded the matter to the executing court for fresh consideration.
A bench of Justices S.V.N. Bhatti and N.V. Anjaria held that the findings recorded by the executing court and the Telangana High Court did not conform to well-established principles of law.
The Court directed the VII Senior Civil Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad, to permit both parties to raise fresh pleas, adduce additional evidence and conduct a fresh inquiry in accordance with law.
The judgment was delivered on October 14 in an appeal filed by Alladin Charities and Zakat Wakf against Mohammed Saleem alias Mohd.
Wajid Ali and another.
The dispute concerns a property measuring approximately 373 square yards, comprising shops at Rikabgunj, Pathergatti, Hyderabad.
The first respondent had filed a suit in 2012 seeking specific performance of an agreement of sale dated February 23, 2001, allegedly executed in his favour.
The suit was decreed ex parte on March 18, 2015, directing execution and registration of a sale deed and granting possession of the property.

When the decree-holder initiated execution proceedings in 2016 to obtain physical possession, Alladin Charities and Zakat Wakf intervened as a third-party objector, claiming that the property belonged to the trust and was Waqf property.

The trust traced its claim to a Farman Mubarak issued by the then Nizam of Hyderabad, which allegedly conveyed the land to Khan Bahadur Ahmed Alladin Nawab Ahmed Nawaz Jung Bahadur, the founder of the Alladin family trusts, for establishing a Waqf for charitable purposes.
It also relied on historical endowment records, a trust deed executed in 1976 and earlier litigation concerning the property.

The executing court dismissed the trust's objection in January 2019, holding, among other things, that it had failed to establish ownership of the specific property covered by the execution proceedings.

stories.headline: Jio's Akash Ambani says services, not tariff hikes, to drive revenue as record IPO nears
stories.title: Jio's Akash Ambani says services, not tariff hikes, to drive revenue as record IPO nears
stories.summary: Ambani said Jio charges about Rs 4.9 per gigabyte against an industry average of Rs 7.5, with customers using 43.7 GB a month.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Ambani said Jio charges about Rs 4.9 per gigabyte against an industry average of Rs 7.5, with customers using 43.7 GB a month.

Jio Platforms plans to raise revenue per customer mainly by selling more services rather than lifting tariffs, though it keeps the option of higher prices, Managing Director Akash Ambani said on Thursday, days before the Reliance Industries unit opens what would be India's largest initial public offering.

"We always have the ability to take up prices," Ambani told a press conference in Mumbai, but the company would rather give customers more services and charge for them than rely on price per gigabyte as its main lever.
Asked whether a tariff increase was coming, he gave no timeline.
He said telecom spending per user as a share of India's per-capita income had roughly halved to about 1% since Jio's 2016 launch, which he called headroom.
Chief Executive Pankaj Pawar said tariffs were only one of several levers.

"We expect a USD 1.4-trillion digital economy by FY31; we will take a huge market share of this," Ambani said, naming mobile, home broadband and enterprise and international services as the growth engines.
He said Jio carries more than 60% of India's wireless data traffic.
New services outside Jio's licensed telecom business, such as a voice-AI feature announced at Reliance's annual meeting, could push its EBITDA margin above the current level.
The margin was 53.3 per cent in April-June, up from about 50% three years ago, he added.

On overseas expansion, Ambani said Jio would offer its in-house network technology to foreign operators as a managed-service partner, not by selling hardware or software licences, and without heavy capital spending.
He said the split between domestic and international revenue would become clear "as we sign on our first customers".
